content.text: I've surveyed the full document — fee/payment terms (§3), exclusivity (§6), and general provisions (§10) — and found no most-favoured-nation, best-pricing, or third-party-offer-matching mechanic in either direction.

input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or best-terms mechanic running in either direction. The economics in §3 (Fees; Payment) are a fixed revenue-share of Net Sales with no obligation on the Company to match third-party terms, to extend to HDI any better pricing or terms granted to others, or to match competing offers; searches for "favorable"/"most favoured"/"best"/"price"/"rates"/"terms and conditions" returned nothing of that character. The only restriction on the Company is the §6.1 exclusivity/non-compete covenant (limited by §6.2), which is a scope restriction rather than an MFN and is addressed under the exclusivity rule, so it is not flagged here. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdening the Customer — so no redline is proposed. Noted only for the record: there is also no MFN in our favour, which is welcome but not required by this rule.
